content:
Maya K.: FYI ACME on Dedicated is seeing sustained 429s for ~7m, says autoscaling didn't kick in fast enough. customer provided logs and request traces.
Jon P.: Thanks — can you paste the error snippets?
Maya K.: From customer: `503 -> 429 backend` and our gateway returns `x-rw-probe-delay: 120s`. they said min_replicas=2, max=20 but only 2 nodes stayed up.
Ryan (ACME): their app: heavy bursts every 30s from batch job; most requests are short 30-60 token generations. Warm pool depleted, then lots of queueing.
Priya S.: Any noisy-tenant signs? throttling in node metrics?
Maya K.: They attached our agent logs: `attach-heartbeat: ok`, then repeated `warm-pool-empty` events, then `probe-timeout -> suppress-scaling` log lines.
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-4321, severity=high, owners=eng-runtime, eng-platform.
Jon P.: Repro steps from customer?
Ryan (ACME): Yes — run this load pattern:
```
for i in 1..50; do curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
done
sleep 25
repeat
```
Maya K.: They reported 6x retries in 2 minutes, most got 429 after the warm pool drained.
Priya S.: Looks like autoscaler suppressed new probes because `probe_backoff` hit threshold after repeated probe timeouts. Need to check `probe_suppression_window` and `min_ready_seconds`.
Jon P.: I pulled the cluster attach logs. Key snippet: `probe: start -> failed (connect timeout) -> suppress due to 3 consecutive failures, cooldown=90s`. So autoscaler waited instead of spinning more capacity.
Priya S.: That cooldown sounds like the probe suppression behavior we added for noisy neighbor protection. For short spike workloads that kills us.
Maya K.: Customer wants immediate mitigation — they want more headroom and fewer 429s.
Jon P.: Quick mitigation options: 1) raise min_replicas to 6 for this customer 2) enable burst_capacity (reserve) 3) lower probe suppression aggressiveness 4) prewarm policy for scheduled bursts. We should recommend 1+4 short term.
Priya S.: Agree. Also check account-level rate limiter — if auth/billing blocked spinups (we saw `billing_hold: false`), so not that.
Maya K.: I set a temporary override: min_replicas=6 on their Dedicated pool and enabled a 5-min prewarm window tied to their scheduled job.
ops-bot: Config change applied by Maya K.: min_replicas override -> 6 for customer ACME (change-id: chg-98321).
Ryan (ACME): Noted — seeing immediate drop in 429s, latency improved to 120ms p50. Thank you.
Jon P.: For long-term: engineering to propose: - adjust probe suppression heuristics to consider warm-pool-empty signal - add a fast-path for burst workloads that uses fast-provisioning slot (small VM/GPU standby) - instrument per-customer warm-pool depth in console.
Priya S.: I'll open a follow-up RFC with metrics we need and recommended defaults for `probe_suppression_window` and `prewarm_triggers`.
Maya K.: Action items: 1) Priya RFC by EOD+2 2) Jon to run a chaos test simulating short spikes across 5 customers to confirm fix 3) support to suggest prewarm or increased min_replicas to customers with scheduled bursts.
Infra-Triage: noted. tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for design review.
Ryan (ACME): Appreciate the rapid patch. Will monitor and report back if anything else pops up.
Jon P.: One more note — logs show occasional `image-pull-delay 12s` during scaleup. Might want to add small warm cache for images on nodes used for Dedicated.
Priya S.: Added to RFC backlog.
Maya K.: Closing customer-facing loop, leaving internal follow-ups open. :white_check_mark:
